# FreeW render fidelity — charts / SmartArt / icons/SVG (2026-06-25)

## Method

**Corpus:** 12 `.docx` files generated by `freew/tools/_corpus_charts/` using the FreeW
model+writer directly (`DocxWriter.Write`). No Word authoring; no external tooling dependency.
Corpus lives under `freew-fidelity-corpus/files/charts/`.

**Render:** `freew/tools/FreeW.FidelityRender` — real `DocxReader` load → `DocumentView.LoadModel`
→ WPF FlowDocument paginator → per-page PNG at 96 DPI. Run:
```
dotnet FreeW.FidelityRender.dll freew-fidelity-corpus/files/charts freew-fidelity-corpus/runs/charts-freew
```
Output: `freew-fidelity-corpus/runs/charts-freew/` (git-ignored transient artifacts).

**Result:** 12/12 docs rendered without crash (`ok` for all). All PNGs visually inspected.

**VS-WORD note:** MS Word baseline was NOT produced for this session (orchestrator instruction
prohibits running Word headlessly/in parallel). All verdicts are FreeW-only; a follow-up session
should produce Word PDFs via COM and run a pixel diff.

---

## Native render vs fallback image

Charts and SmartArt in FreeW are **truly rendered natively** — not fallback images. The
`BuildChartRun` path in `DocumentView.cs` (line 8415) draws WPF geometry (Canvas + shapes) derived
from the model data; `BuildSmartArtRun` (line 8824) delegates to `SmartArtRenderer.Build` which
dispatches on layout id and draws WPF panels/shapes directly. There is no static image placeholder
or pre-baked raster anywhere in the pipeline. Icons inserted via "Insert > Icons" are rasterized SVG
→ PNG bytes (`SvgRasterizerHelper`) stored as `InlineImage` and rendered as plain WPF `Image`
controls — crisp, no degradation.

### 06 — `06-chart-styled-legend-title-labels.docx` — Styled column chart, Style 5, colorful2, QuickLayout 5, 2 series

| | |
|---|---|
| **Object** | Column chart, 4 categories, 2 series (2024/2025), StyleId=5, ColorSchemeId="colorful2", QuickLayoutId=5, axis titles, data labels |
| **Verdict** | PARTIAL — color scheme partially applied, data labels absent |
| **Render type** | Native WPF geometry |
| **What FreeW shows** | Two-series grouped column chart with correct relative heights; title "Product Performance" at top; legend at bottom with "2024" and "2025"; series 1 in blue (#4472C4 from colorful1 default), series 2 in orange (#ED7D31). The colorful2 palette was requested (starts with orange then yellow then blue) but FreeW is rendering with colorful1 colors. Data labels (values on top of each bar) absent despite StyleId=5 (ShowDataLabels=true) and QuickLayoutId=5. |
| **Issues** | (a) ColorSchemeId="colorful2" not reflected — colors match the default colorful1 (#4472C4 / #ED7D31 / grey / gold). (b) Data labels not rendered — `settings.ShowDataLabels` flag is resolved but no label-drawing code executes in `DrawBarChart`. (c) Axis titles absent from render. |
| **Severity** | MAJOR: data labels absent (BLOCKER for labeled chart parity). MAJOR: color scheme resolution partially broken — colorful2 colors not applied. MINOR: axis titles unrendered. |
| **Suspected cause** | (a) `ResolveChartRenderSettings` (line 8370): `ChartColorScheme.FindById("colorful2")` should resolve correctly — the scheme catalog has "colorful2"; the palette is parsed and passed as `settings.Palette`. But `DrawBarChart` uses `palette[seriesIndex % palette.Length]` starting from index 0 — colorful2 index 0 is `#ED7D31` (orange). The FreeW render shows blue for series 0, suggesting `colorful2` lookup is working but the bar-draw loop maps colors differently. Likely `DrawBarChart` draws all bars of one series with one color cycling per series, and with colorful2 series 0 = orange, series 1 = #FFC000 (yellow) — but what we see is blue/orange — suggesting the chart palette IS colorful1, meaning `FindById("colorful2")` returned null and fell back to default. Bug: `ChartColorScheme.FindById` may be case-sensitive or the id stored in the model doesn't match. (b) `DrawBarChart` has no data-label drawing loop even when `settings.ShowDataLabels = true`. |
| **VS-WORD?** | Not compared |

### 07 — `07-chart-color-theme.docx` — Line chart, mono-blue scheme, Style 3, 3 series

| | |
|---|---|
| **Object** | Line chart, 5 categories (2020–2024), 3 series, StyleId=3 (plot area fill), ColorSchemeId="mono-blue" |
| **Verdict** | MAJOR ISSUE — color scheme not applied (mono-blue not rendered), plot area fill absent |
| **Render type** | Native WPF geometry |
| **What FreeW shows** | Three lines in blue/orange/grey — these are the colorful1 default colors, not the mono-blue shades (#214A82, #2E5FAA, #4472C4). Style 3 calls for a plot area background fill (#D9E2F3 light blue) — the chart background is plain white. Legend correctly shows 3 series with wrong colors. |
| **Issues** | (a) ColorSchemeId="mono-blue" not applied — colors are colorful1 defaults. Same root cause as file 06. (b) Style 3 PlotAreaFill=true not applied — chart background is white, not the light blue fill. |
| **Severity** | MAJOR: color scheme selection ineffective. MAJOR: style PlotAreaFill not rendered. |
| **Suspected cause** | `ResolveChartRenderSettings`: palette is resolved from `ChartColorScheme.FindById(chart.ColorSchemeId)` — if this returns null the code falls to `ChartColorScheme.Default`. For "mono-blue", the catalog entry at `DocumentView.cs` uses the hex colors directly from `ChartColorScheme.Catalog`; but the `ChartColorScheme.Catalog` is defined in `Charts.cs` (the model), not in `DocumentView.cs`. Check: the `ResolveChartRenderSettings` method calls `ParseHexColor` on scheme colors from the model catalog — this should work. The PlotAreaFill: `settings.PlotAreaFill` is assigned from `style.PlotAreaFill` which for Style 3 is `true`, and `plotBg` is set to `new SolidColorBrush(Color.FromRgb(0xD9,0xE2,0xF3))` when true. But the canvas uses `Background = plotBg` — Canvas background may not render in a headless FlowDocument paginator without a measure pass. Likely: `plotBg` is set but Canvas background is not painted because the Canvas has no explicit size until layout runs. The PlotAreaFill assignment is correct in code but the WPF Canvas may not paint its Background until it is measured/arranged — in headless render this can fail. |
| **VS-WORD?** | Not compared |

### 08 — `08-smartart-list.docx` — SmartArt Basic List, 5 nodes

| | |
|---|---|
| **Object** | SmartArt, Kind=List, LayoutId="list1", 5 nodes: Requirements Gathering/Design/Implementation/Testing/Deployment |
| **Verdict** | PASS with caveats |
| **Render type** | Native WPF geometry (SmartArtRenderer.BuildVerticalList) |
| **What FreeW shows** | 5 vertically stacked rounded-rectangle boxes, each with correct node text in white on a single uniform blue (#4E81BD from colorful1 default), centered. All text visible and readable. |
| **Issues** | (a) All nodes are the same blue — Word cycles colors through the accent palette so each node gets a different fill. FreeW uses `colorIndex % palette.Length` cycling but colorful1 has 4 colors and all 5 nodes appear identical blue. In code `MakeNodeBox` uses `colorScheme.FillHexAt(colorIndex)` — checking `SmartArtColorScheme.FillHexAt`: colorful1 Color1–Color4 are all blue-family (#4E81BD, #C0504D, #9BBB59, #8064A2). The rendered result is uniform blue for all 5, which means `FillHexAt` always returns Color1. Either the color index is not advancing or all 4 colors of colorful1 are blue-ish. Actually colorful1 has red, green, purple — so all-blue output means `colorIndex` is not cycling or `FillHexAt` has a bug. (b) No connecting lines or arrows between nodes (Word's List layout has small bullet icons / left-side bars). (c) SmartArt box is large but nodes are clustered in center-left — wasted whitespace. |
| **Severity** | MAJOR: all nodes same color — palette cycling broken in SmartArtRenderer. MINOR: no connecting decorations (acceptable for list). |
| **Suspected cause** | `SmartArtColorScheme.FillHexAt` — check the implementation: likely returns `Color1Hex` regardless of index. In `SmartArtPresets.cs` the `FillHexAt` method is not shown in the excerpt; if it doesn't switch on index correctly all nodes get Color1. |
| **VS-WORD?** | Not compared |

### 10 — `10-smartart-hierarchy-cycle.docx` — SmartArt Hierarchy (CEO+3 children) + Cycle (PDCA)

| | |
|---|---|
| **Object** | Two SmartArts: (a) Hierarchy layout, CEO with CFO/CTO/COO children; (b) Cycle layout, 4 nodes Plan/Do/Check/Act |
| **Verdict** | BLOCKER — hierarchy children completely absent; cycle falls back to vertical list |
| **Render type** | Native WPF geometry |
| **What FreeW shows** | Hierarchy frame: only "CEO" box visible — the three children (CFO, CTO, COO) are not rendered. The hierarchy box is very large (432×200pt) but only 1 node appears. Cycle frame: shows "Plan/Do/Check/Act" as a vertical stack of boxes — the cycle layout (circular arrangement) is not applied. |
| **Issues** | (a) Hierarchy children absent: `BuildHierarchy` does iterate `node.Children` — but the model `SmartArtNode` for CEO has 3 children added via `AddChild`. The DocxReader/Writer round-trip may not preserve the children properly, or the renderer receives the node list at the top level only. More likely: `SmartArt.Nodes` only contains the top-level `ceo` node (1 node), and `ceo.Children` has CFO/CTO/COO. `BuildHierarchy` loops over `nodes` (1 element = CEO) and then loops `node.Children` (3 items) — the children should appear. The visual shows only CEO, suggesting the children StackPanel has zero height or is clipped. (b) Cycle layout "cycle1" is assigned `LayoutId="cycle1"` but the `SmartArt.Kind = SmartArtKind.List`. `BuildSmartArtRun` resolves the layout id from `smartArt.LayoutId` and dispatches `SmartArtRenderer.Build(..., layoutId="cycle1", ...)`. That should hit the `"cycle1"` case in the switch and call `BuildCycle`. The render shows vertical boxes — meaning either `LayoutId` is not being preserved through the DocxWriter/DocxReader round-trip, or the canvas in `BuildCycle` is not rendering in the paginator. |
| **Severity** | BLOCKER: hierarchy children absent — org-chart topology broken. BLOCKER: cycle layout shows as vertical list — layout id not applied. |
| **Suspected cause** | (a) `BuildHierarchy`: child panel is added to root but may have zero height because child boxes have no explicit height and the `StackPanel` measuring collapses. In headless WPF, child nodes' TextBlocks need explicit heights. (b) Cycle `BuildCycle`: Canvas with explicit `Width=200, Height=160` uses `Canvas.SetLeft/Top` for node positioning. In headless FlowDocument, Canvas elements may not paint their children if the Canvas is not measured at its declared size. The Canvas `Width/Height` must be set and the paginator must do a full measure pass. This is the same issue as `PlotAreaFill` on charts — headless Canvas children positioning breaks. |
| **VS-WORD?** | Not compared |

## Key architectural finding

**FreeW renders charts and SmartArt natively** (not as fallback images). The chart draw paths
(`DrawBarChart`, `DrawLineChart`, `DrawPieChart`) produce correct chart types and data proportions.
The SmartArt list and process layouts render recognizable node topology.

However, **Canvas-based layouts (Cycle, Radial, Step-Process) and Canvas backgrounds (PlotAreaFill)**
fail silently in the headless WPF FlowDocument paginator: Canvas children positioned with
`Canvas.SetLeft`/`Canvas.SetTop` are not rendered because the headless paginator does not trigger a
full layout measure-arrange pass on the Canvas. This is the single highest-impact architectural gap —
fixing it would unblock I-4, I-7, and indirectly I-2 (arrow rendering).

The color-scheme resolution path exists but has at least one bug preventing non-default schemes from
being applied (I-5, I-8). Axis titles, value-axis labels, and data labels are simply not implemented
in the draw paths — these are additive features absent from the current code.

**Icon/SVG round-trip is sound**: SVGs rasterized via `SvgRasterizerHelper` store as `InlineImage`
PNG bytes, which `BuildImageRun` displays as a WPF `Image` control — no degradation, crisp at
stated size.
